page.layout: One column of text on the page, with a numbered entry at its left edge and a short marginal note at the right, beside the entry "9." Running head at top. Gathering mark and page number at the foot.

main_text.p: Fides bellica quomodo hosti servanda in-violata: nempe
Legatos, amicos, obsides hostium non violando.
9. In Principe domi sit sanctitas; fortitudo in armis: utrobique prudentia. Hic non immerito omnimodâ virtute[?]: quaeritur:
Sanctitas in Principe cur necessaria? Nimirum, Ut suam apud subditos auctoritate con-servet: & diutius atque tutius imperet.
Cur tyranni imperium sit instabile? Ut subditos iustius regat:
Ne aliis exemplo suo noceat. Hic quo-que notandum,
Fortitudo in armis cur necessaria Principi?
Dignitatum tituli quomodo Principem officii sui moneant.
Timiditatem & socordiam viro Principi esse indignam.
Pacem turpem Principi forti non esse re-dimendam: nec bellum semper fu-giendum.
Principis in bello praesentia quantū con-ducat.

page.notes: The marginal words "omnimodâ" and "virtute" are set in the right margin beside the entry "9."; the second word is partly obscured and its ending is uncertain. The entry "9." is printed in the left margin. Long s in "sanctitas" is printed as a long-s form in the scan; read as sanctitas. The line "Hic non immerito" carries a marginal word that runs beside the text line. The running head and page number are printed as shown.
